text:
mina: Hey team, model-serving pods in the us-west-2 GPU pool started returning grpc UNAVAILABLE / connect timeouts ~09:05 UTC during batch loads. Error rate ~18% for a 20m window. Suspect DNS because logs show repeated resolve errors.

mina: excerpt from pod logs: 
```
E0318 09:05:12.123 1 resolver.go:102] lookup model-registry.default.svc.cluster.local on 10.96.0.10:53: read udp 10.40.2.13:49852->10.96.0.10:53: i/o timeout
E0318 09:05:12.124 1 transport.go:345] grpc: addrConn.createTransport failed to connect to {model-registry.default.svc.cluster.local:8080 0  <nil>} last error: connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial udp 10.96.0.10:53: i/o timeout"
```

jasper: Noticed a small MTU tweak landed on the GPU node pools yesterday for RDMA tuning. Could be fragmentation causing coredns UDP drops.

anita: CoreDNS pods show CPU spikes and a lot of "error: read udp" messages in kube-system. Node-local-dns cache on each node also has high restart counts on some nodes.

devops-sam: Confirming: RDMA enablement + mtu=9000 change applied to a subset of nodes at 02:00 UTC. If some parts of the path still use 1500, UDP fragmentation could cause those i/o timeouts.

mina: Running quick checks now: 
```
# on a affected node
$ iperf3 -c 10.96.0.10 -u -b 100M -t 10
# tcpdump for DNS failures
$ sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 53 and '(udp[10:2] & 0x1fff) != 0' -w dns_frag.pcap
```

jasper: Also run `kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/node-local-dns -c node-local-dns --since=15m` and `kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/coredns --since=15m` — paste any stack traces.

anita: pasted CoreDNS errors: 
```
2026-03-18T09:04:58.321Z [ERROR] plugin/errors: 2 model-registry.default.svc.cluster.local. A: read udp 10.96.0.10:53->10.40.2.13:49852: i/o timeout
2026-03-18T09:05:10.112Z [WARN] metrics: request_duration_seconds bucket overflow
```

devops-sam: Quick mitigation idea: force TCP for DNS queries from node-local cache to CoreDNS (node-resolv.conf can use `options use-vc`) or increase MTU consistency across infra. Also bump node-local-dns cache TTL to reduce queries during spikes.

mina: Can we flip node-local-dns to TCP for the cluster as a test? Seems lower perf but more reliable for large UDP frag.

jasper: We can patch the `node-local-dns` daemonset to add `- -conf` and rewrite to force `use-vc` in resolv.conf via configmap. Patch looks like: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  resolv.conf: "options single-request-reopen use-vc"
```

anita: For immediate relief, I'm restarting node-local-dns on the most affected nodes (node-*-gpu-3, node-*-gpu-7). Will watch error rate.

sre-bot: INCIDENT: DNS spikes detected in us-west-2 GPU pool. Alert #INC-20260318-12 created and assigned to eng-infra.

mina: After restarting node-local-dns on 6 nodes, error rate dropped to ~2% in the last 5m. Still seeing a couple of backoffs when batches hit new model fetches.

devops-sam: Next steps: 1) Rollback partial MTU change for RDMA nodes until we confirm fragmentation path. 2) Patch node-local-dns to prefer TCP to CoreDNS. 3) Scale CoreDNS to +2 replicas in us-west-2. 4) Run cluster-wide iperf + frag tests across AZs.

jasper: I'll take step 1 (rollback MTU for the affected pool). Mina, can you coordinate the node-local-dns patch and run the iperf matrix? I'll schedule the rollback in a 30m maintenance window.

mina: On it — will open a PR for the node-local-dns config and kick off iperf matrix. Posting results here when done.

anita: Filing a short postmortem template now and capturing which model-serving jobs timed out (batch ingest 03:50-09:15 UTC).

sre-bot: NOTE: follow-up runbook suggestions: add DNS health checks to model-serving readiness probe, and add fallback to service mesh mTLS hostnames if DNS fails.

mina: Thanks — will add runbook entries. Will update once iperf + tcpdump captures are in.
